title: Meta’s Muse is now on iPad with more app connections
key_facts: Meta's Muse is available on iPad, announced in an Oct. 7 Threads post, after its Sept. 8 mobile debut.
Muse is a free agentic AI assistant that can book reservations, order groceries, manage appointments and make purchases; users choose which accounts to connect.
Muse has surpassed an estimated 6.6 million installs.
App Store release notes list connectors for Asana, Canva, Dropbox, Figma, QuickBooks, GitHub, Klaviyo, Zoom and Meta ad accounts, plus Granola and Notion.
Meta says users can give Muse a business goal, such as planning marketing content or building client pitches, with their approval; the small-business push was announced on Sept. 29.
More retail partners were announced at Connect: Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Walmart and Wayfair.
Websites can block an AI assistant as a bot; Meta is working on an open standard for agents to identify themselves, but Amazon has already taken steps to block Muse.

Earlier concerns: one user said Muse shared his home address and arranged a Facebook Marketplace pickup without checking; columnist Jason Aten alleged it read private messages he had not authorised; Wired reportedly found instructions for Muse to compile profiles of users' friends, family and colleagues.

why_it_matters_hint: A month-old consumer AI agent keeps widening what it can reach, while retailers and critics push back.
